guidelineVersions: NICE NG12 Suspected cancer (last updated 15 April 2026)
NICE NG231 Barrett's oesophagus and stage 1 oesophageal adenocarcinoma (February 2023)
NICE NG83 Oesophago-gastric cancer (last updated 4 July 2023)

brief.scenario: Douglas Aitken, 62, has had three months of progressive dysphagia to solids and 7 kg weight loss. He has had reflux for 15 years. The examiner will read out his endoscopy, histology and staging findings in stages.
brief.task: Interpret the findings, explain the underlying pathology, and outline staging and management. You may be asked about Barrett's surveillance.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Refer, read the endoscopy, name the pathology, stage, then treat in a specialist MDT.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Quoting old Barrett's intervals: low-grade dysplasia now means ablation, not 6-monthly endoscopy.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Dysphagia at any age needs a suspected cancer pathway referral."

grid.label: Referral
grid.fail: Treats dysphagia as reflux with a PPI trial.
grid.pass: Dysphagia at any age: suspected cancer pathway referral for oesophageal cancer.
grid.high: Adds the other trigger: aged 55 or over with weight loss plus upper abdominal pain, reflux or dyspepsia.

grid.label: Reading the endoscopy
grid.fail: Cannot define Barrett's or read the Prague score.
grid.pass: Barrett's: columnar epithelium at least 1 cm above the gastro-oesophageal junction, confirmed on biopsy. C3M7 is long-segment Barrett's.
grid.high: Explains C is circumferential and M maximum extent in cm; Seattle protocol: quadrant biopsies every 2 cm plus targeted biopsies.

grid.label: Pathology and risk
grid.fail: Confuses adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma risk factors.
grid.pass: Adenocarcinoma: distal, reflux, Barrett's, obesity, men. Squamous: upper or middle third, smoking, alcohol. Metaplasia, dysplasia, carcinoma sequence.
grid.high: Non-dysplastic Barrett's progresses to cancer in about 0.3% per year, roughly 1 in 300.

grid.label: Staging
grid.pass: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis first; then PET-CT if suitable for radical treatment.
grid.high: Endoscopic ultrasound or staging laparoscopy only if it will change management; endoscopic resection to stage suspected T1 disease.

grid.label: Treatment
grid.fail: Offers surgery alone, or treats outside a specialist team.
grid.pass: Specialist OG cancer MDT. Localised adenocarcinoma: chemotherapy before (or before and after) surgery, or chemoradiotherapy before surgery, then oesophagectomy.
grid.high: Adds dietitian and specialist nurse; adjuvant nivolumab for residual disease after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy; stenting or radiotherapy if palliative.

grid.label: Barrett's surveillance
grid.fail: Gives one interval for all Barrett's.
grid.pass: Long segment (3 cm or more): every 2 to 3 years. Short segment with intestinal metaplasia: every 3 to 5 years.
grid.high: Short segment without intestinal metaplasia on 2 endoscopies: no surveillance. Tailors within the range by age, sex, family history and smoking.

grid.label: Dysplasia
grid.fail: Plans oesophagectomy for all high-grade dysplasia, or only surveillance.
grid.pass: High-grade: endoscopic resection of visible lesions, then ablation. Low-grade on 2 endoscopies, confirmed by 2 GI pathologists: radiofrequency ablation.
grid.high: Indefinite dysplasia: repeat at 6 months after optimising acid suppression. T1b with deep invasion or lymphovascular invasion: oesophagectomy if fit.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: His GP calls. How should he be referred?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Start omeprazole and refer routinely if it doesn't settle.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The report says Prague C3M7. What does that mean?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'm not sure. Some kind of reflux grade.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What are the risk factors for this cancer?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Smoking and alcohol, like squamous cell.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: His brother has Barrett's. How often should he be scoped?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: And if it shows high-grade dysplasia?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Dysphagia at any age needs a suspected cancer pathway referral.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Barrett's is columnar epithelium at least 1 cm above the gastro-oesophageal junction, confirmed on biopsy. C3M7 is long-segment Barrett's, with a mass at the distal end. Goblet cells in the columnar mucosa mean intestinal metaplasia.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Adenocarcinoma, from reflux causing metaplasia, then dysplasia, then carcinoma. Obesity and male sex add risk. Squamous cancers are higher up and linked to smoking and alcohol.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis, then PET-CT if he's suitable for radical treatment.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Discuss at the specialist MDT. Chemotherapy or chemoradiotherapy before surgery, then oesophagectomy.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: His brother has 5 cm of Barrett's without dysplasia.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Long segment, so every 2 to 3 years. A short segment with intestinal metaplasia would be every 3 to 5 years.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: High-grade: endoscopic resection of visible lesions then ablation. Low-grade confirmed on two endoscopies by two GI pathologists: radiofrequency ablation.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: He also meets the second trigger: over 55 with weight loss and reflux.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How is the Barrett's segment measured?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: C is the circumferential extent and M the maximum extent, in cm above the junction. Surveillance uses the Seattle protocol: quadrant biopsies every 2 cm plus targeted biopsies.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How often does Barrett's become cancer?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Without dysplasia, about 0.3% per year, roughly 1 in 300.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Would you do an endoscopic ultrasound?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Only if it would change management. Staging laparoscopy likewise. If it looked like a T1 lesion, endoscopic resection itself stages it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A dietitian and specialist nurse from the start. If he has chemoradiotherapy and there's residual disease after resection, adjuvant nivolumab. If he's unfit, stenting or radiotherapy for palliation.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: His brother's segment is 2 cm without intestinal metaplasia.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: If that's confirmed on two endoscopies, no surveillance. Otherwise I'd tailor the interval to age, sex, family history and smoking.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Optimise acid suppression and repeat at 6 months. If a resected lesion is T1b with deep submucosal or lymphovascular invasion, he'd need oesophagectomy if fit.

failures.move: Giving a PPI trial for new dysphagia.
failures.consequence: Delays the diagnosis of oesophageal cancer.
Exposes a patient with metastases to a major operation that cannot cure him.

failures.move: Surveillance alone for confirmed low-grade dysplasia.
failures.consequence: NICE now offers radiofrequency ablation once the diagnosis is confirmed.
Over-investigates low-risk patients; intervals depend on segment length and metaplasia.

recovery.line: Long segment 2 to 3 years, short with metaplasia 3 to 5, short without none.
Staging first, then a specialist MDT decision.

knowledge.fact: Dysphagia at any age: suspected cancer pathway referral.
Barrett's: columnar epithelium 1 cm or more above the junction, confirmed histologically.
Annual adenocarcinoma risk in Barrett's was 0.12% in a Danish national cohort, lower than older estimates.
Surveillance: 3 cm or more every 2 to 3 years; under 3 cm with metaplasia every 3 to 5 years.
Localised adenocarcinoma for resection: chemotherapy before, or before and after, surgery, or preoperative chemoradiotherapy.
Prague C&M: circumferential and maximum extent of Barrett's in cm.

recall.think: Dysphagia with weight loss is cancer until proven otherwise.
recall.say: "Suspected cancer pathway referral, then stage before any decision."
do: Refer on the suspected cancer pathway
CT, then PET-CT if radical treatment possible
Specialist MDT: neoadjuvant therapy then oesophagectomy

numbers.meaning: surveillance: long segment / short segment with metaplasia

recall.trap: Low-grade dysplasia confirmed twice now means ablation, not watching.
recall.finish: Neoadjuvant therapy and oesophagectomy in a specialist centre; endoscopic therapy for dysplasia and T1a.

partner.opening: Mr Aitken's GP has referred him. How should a patient like this be referred? I will then read out his endoscopy findings.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for the endoscopy report
reveals.finding: Read out: the endoscopy shows salmon-pink, velvety mucosa replacing the pale squamous lining of the distal oesophagus. It extends circumferentially for 3 cm above the gastro-oesophageal junction, with tongues reaching 7 cm above it: Prague C3M7. There is an irregular, ulcerated mass at 35 to 38 cm, just above the gastro-oesophageal junction.

Read out: biopsies of the mass show invasive adenocarcinoma. Biopsies of the flat salmon-pink mucosa show columnar epithelium in place of the normal stratified squamous lining, with scattered goblet cells: rounded cells with a large, clear, mucin-filled vacuole.
Read out: CT: thickened distal oesophagus, one enlarged paraoesophageal node, no metastases. PET-CT: no distant uptake.

push.question: How should the GP refer him?
push.expect: Suspected cancer pathway referral for dysphagia.

push.question: What does C3M7 mean?
push.expect: Circumferential 3 cm, maximum 7 cm: long-segment Barrett's.

push.question: How would you stage him?
push.expect: CT chest, abdomen, pelvis, then PET-CT.

push.question: What treatment will the MDT consider?
push.expect: Neoadjuvant or perioperative chemotherapy, or preoperative chemoradiotherapy, then oesophagectomy.

push.question: How often should Barrett's be surveyed?
push.expect: 3 cm or more: 2 to 3 years; under 3 cm with metaplasia: 3 to 5 years.

push.question: What if low-grade dysplasia is found?
push.expect: Confirm on 2 endoscopies and by 2 pathologists, then radiofrequency ablation.

curveballs.prompt: Should he take aspirin to stop progression?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No. NICE advises against aspirin for this purpose.

curveballs.prompt: Would anti-reflux surgery prevent cancer in Barrett's?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No. It is not offered to prevent progression; only for reflux symptoms under the GORD guidance.

curveballs.prompt: The resected lesion is T1a with clear margins.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Endoscopic resection is first-line; ablate residual Barrett's and follow up endoscopically.
